land.text: the Kingdom of Jibei: 'northern Shandong' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

predecessors.note: Xiang Yu 'divided Qi into Qi, Jiaodong, and Jibei' (Tian Rong page); Jibei's land came out of the Qi lands, which the ea-01 qi dossier notes. Tian An is a Qi rebel leader (Eighteen Kingdoms table).

land.text: the Kingdom of Jibei: 'northern Shandong' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

successors.note: Tian Rong, who 'killed Tian Fu, Tian An' (Tian Rong page), reunited the three Qis; the qi dossier (ea-01) covers only the Tian Du Qi of 206-204, so the annexation is not in its keyframes.

capitals.name: Bogao (Tai'an area)
capitals.note: Not on any page opened: no page names Jibei's capital. Bogao is the traditional seat of Tian An; unverified. Coordinates are modern Tai'an.

rulers.name: Tian An
rulers.title: King of Jibei
rulers.note: 'Tian An, a Qi rebel leader' (Eighteen Kingdoms table); killed on Tian Rong's orders by Peng Yue (Timeline, 206).

correction.text: belongs to the revived Qi of 208-207, not to the Kingdom of Jibei; no page gives it a boundary

keyframe_review.note: Not Jibei: the shape (145,995 km2; 786 grid cells, 96 percent of them in Shandong, 87 percent of the province) is the whole of Shandong in 208-207, whereas the Eighteen Kingdoms table gives Jibei only 'northern Shandong', and Jibei was created by Xiang Yu in 206. The land belongs to the revived Qi of 208-207, for which Cliopatria has no row (its Qi row skips 218-207); the qin-dynasty dossier records the loss to 'qi'. No page opened gives the revived Qi's land or kings (the Tian Rong page has only the 206 division).

correction.text: the Kingdom of Jibei: 'northern Shandong' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (44,210 km2; 239 grid cells, 85 percent of them in Shandong, 36 in Hebei) and in line with the table's 'northern Shandong'; the page gives no area and does not mention the Hebei cells. The years change: the kingdom lasted 206 only, because the Timeline page has Tian Rong's general Peng Yue conquer it and kill Tian An in 206; Cliopatria carries the shape to 204. After 206 the land is Tian Rong's Qi.

region.text: the Kingdom of Jibei: 'northern Shandong' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Tian An King of Jibei. The Eighteen Kingdoms were 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE'; table: Jibei, Tian An, 'northern Shandong'. The Tian Rong page: Xiang Yu 'divided Qi into Qi, Jiaodong, and Jibei, appointing Tian Du, Tian Fu, and Tian An as kings'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Jibei: 'northern Shandong' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 206: Tian Rong conquers Jibei. Timeline, 206 BC: 'Tian Rong sends Peng Yue to conquer the Kingdom of Jibei and kill its king, Tian An.' The Chu-Han Contention page: 'Merely six months after Qin dynasty's collapse' Tian Rong killed the kings of Jiaodong and Jibei; the Tian Rong page dates his revolt to 205 and the Xiang Yu page to 'some months' after late 206.

region.text: the Kingdom of Jibei: 'northern Shandong' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 206: the Kingdom of Jibei ends with Tian An. The Eighteen Kingdoms table gives no fate; the Timeline names the conqueror.

wars.name: Tian Rong's conquest of Jibei and Jiaodong

zones.text: the Kingdom of Jibei: 'northern Shandong' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

wars.outcome: Tian Rong killed the kings of Jiaodong and Jibei (Tian Fu and Tian An on the Timeline) and drove out Tian Du, reuniting the three Qis; Xiang Yu then campaigned in Qi (Timeline: 205).
wars.note: The Chu-Han Contention page names the Jiaodong king Tian Shi where the table and the Timeline name Tian Fu; the Tian Rong page dates the revolt 205.

certainty.note: 'Northern Shandong' is all the pages say; Cliopatria's outline is an approximation.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Jibei' (208-204) is two things: jibei_-208 (208-207) is the whole of Shandong, the revived Qi, and is marked wrong here; jibei_-206 (206-204) is the Kingdom of Jibei, which the pages end in 206 (Tian Rong's conquest) or 205 (the Tian Rong page); 206 used. The revived Qi of 208-207 (Tian Dan, Tian Rong, Tian Fu/Tian Shi) has no dossier and no shape in Cliopatria's Qi row: counterparts_needing_dossiers asks the qi owner (ea-01) to extend the qi dossier to cover Shandong 208-207, or a rebel dossier. The kingdoms of Jibei and Jiaodong were absorbed by Tian Rong's Qi, but ea-01's qi keyframes hold only 60,000 km2 of southern Shandong for 206-204, so Jibei's and Jiaodong's lands are un-owned after 206 unless the qi dossier is extended. Not on any page: Jibei's capital (Bogao from tradition, flagged), boundary, area, month. The Tian An URL https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tian_An failed (not found); the Tian Rong page is thin and its lead gives Tian Rong's death as 203 by Han Xin, which conflicts with the Timeline (205) and was not used. Pages beyond the hubs (Eighteen Kingdoms, Chu-Han Contention, Timeline): Tian Rong only, within the budget. Gazetteer: no new names.
